$comment: What holds for each specification under spec/. The texts under spec/*.md are frozen at the casting named here and are not edited, apart from the status block at their top. scripts/build-spec-status.mjs writes that block, the status section of README.md and the document table of apps/site/src/content/docs/reference/specifications.md from this file; `npm run validate` checks them with --check, and checks each frozen text against its `textDigest`. Where a text and the library disagree, the library with its vectors and flows holds until the text is brought up to date.

statuses.built: the library implements this part; it has not been reconciled with the text rule by rule, so single rules may differ
statuses.partly-built: implemented in the library in part; the note says which part
statuses.built-differently: implemented in the library with a reading other than the text; `ref` names where the reading is stated
statuses.direction-changed: the planned model differs from the text; `ref` names the direction note
statuses.not-verified: no evidence was checked for this part

parts.title: The `replyTo` of a sent message (RLTP-MSG-5120)
parts.note: The library checks only that `replyTo` has the form of a UUID. That it names an earlier message of the same relationship is the sending application's to ensure; the library keeps no history of sent messages to check it against.

parts.title: Holding a message until its tuple is ready
parts.note: `sendMessage` answers `not-ready`; keeping the message until it can be sent is the application's task.

parts.title: Sending, with the sender lifetime (rule 5110)
parts.note: The sender lifetime is a local give-up time on the outbox entry, not a field of the document. For a message the counterpart does not hold, the library's retry horizon of at most P90D ends first, as `failed(expired-by-adapter-policy)`, so the engine's outcome `failed(task-expired)` is unreachable for `message/0.1`; an entry with `held: true` is given up at neither.
